question: Can a sequence to sequence model built entirely from convolutions match or beat deep recurrent (LSTM/GRU) models on large translation benchmarks while being much faster?
hypothesis: Convolutions with GLUs, residual connections and per-layer attention can outperform recurrent seq2seq with easier optimisation and parallel computation over all positions.
contributions: First fully convolutional seq2seq architecture (encoder and decoder) with GLUs, residual connections and position embeddings
Multi-step attention: a separate attention module in every decoder layer
Variance-preserving normalisation (scaling by sqrt(0.5), m*sqrt(1/m)) and GLU/dropout-aware weight initialisation
New state of the art on WMT'16 En-Ro, and beating GNMT on WMT'14 En-De and En-Fr at roughly an order of magnitude faster generation

method.summary: Encoder and decoder are stacks of 1-D convolution blocks with GLU non-linearity and residual connections; word plus absolute position embeddings feed in; each decoder layer has dot-product attention over encoder outputs plus input embeddings. Trained with token-level likelihood on WMT translation and Gigaword summarization.
method.task: machine translation (En-Ro, En-De, En-Fr) and abstractive sentence summarization

datasets.name: WMT'16 English-Romanian
datasets.split: eval on newstest2016; 0.5-1% of train as validation
datasets.source: Sennrich et al. 2016b data plus back-translated data
datasets.preprocessing: Sennrich et al. scripts; word vocab 200K source / 80K target, or joint BPE 40K

datasets.name: WMT'14 English-German
datasets.split: test newstest2014; length-norm tuned on newstest2015; 0.5-1% validation

datasets.name: WMT'14 English-French
datasets.size: 35.5M sentence pairs (from 36M; >175 words and length ratio >1.5 removed)
datasets.split: test newstest2014; speed eval on dev newstest2012+2013 (6003 sentences)

datasets.name: Gigaword
datasets.split: eval on DUC-2004 (500 article-title pairs) and a 2000-pair Gigaword test set
datasets.source: Graff et al. 2003; preprocessing of Rush et al. 2015
datasets.preprocessing: 30K word vocab source and target; outputs required to be at least 14 words

models.name: ConvS2S En-Ro
models.architecture: fully convolutional seq2seq, GLU, residual, multi-step attention

models.name: ConvS2S En-De
models.hidden: 512 in first ten layers, 768 in next three, final two layers 2048 units (linear, width 1)

models.name: ConvS2S En-Fr
models.hidden: 512 first five layers, 768 next four, 1024 next three, final two layers 2048 and 4096 (linear, width 1)
models.context: effective context size of only 25 words

models.name: ConvS2S ablation model
models.vocab: target 160K words with vocabulary selection (~20K avg per batch)

models.name: ByteNet, Luong LSTM, Zhou, Shazeer MoE, Ha hypernetworks, Shen RNN, WFE

training.optimizer: Nesterov accelerated gradient, momentum 0.99, gradient renormalised when norm exceeds 0.1
training.lr_schedule: when validation perplexity stops improving, reduce lr by an order of magnitude after each epoch until below 1e-4
training.batch_size: 64 sentences unless stated (48 En-De, 32 per worker x 8 GPUs En-Fr, 128 summarisation); capped by max words per batch with splitting
training.regularisation: dropout on embeddings, decoder output and input to conv blocks (retain probability p; rate value not stated); weight normalisation on all layers except lookup tables
training.hardware: single Nvidia M40 GPU; En-Fr on up to 8 GPUs synchronously with NCCL
training.compute: En-Ro 6-7.5 days on 1 GPU; En-De 18.5 days on 1 GPU; En-Fr about 37 days on 8 GPUs; summarisation one night on 1 GPU
training.seeds: three runs differing only in initial random seed, averaged

other.init: embeddings normal mean 0 std 0.1; layers before GLU N(0,sqrt(4p/n_l)), others N(0,sqrt(p/n_l)); biases zero
other.residual scaling: multiply sum of input and output by sqrt(0.5)
other.encoder gradient: scaled by number of attention mechanisms (source embeddings excluded)
other.gradient normalisation: by number of non-padding tokens per mini-batch

inference.decoding: beam search, beam width 5; log-likelihood divided by length |y| (En-De: |y|^alpha with alpha tuned on newstest2015, value not stated)

parameters.unknown_word_replacement: word-based models only: replace UNK by dictionary translation (fast_align most-frequent alignment) of source word with max attention averaged over layers, else copy
parameters.speed_batch: up to 128 sentences of equal length; unchanged convolution states copied (shifted) not recomputed

metrics.name: BLEU
metrics.definition: case-sensitive tokenized BLEU (multi-bleu.perl); detokenized (mteval-v13a) for En-Ro

metrics.name: ROUGE-1/2/L
metrics.definition: recall-based on DUC-2004; F1 on Gigaword

metrics.name: generation time
metrics.definition: seconds to translate 6003-sentence En-Fr dev set

eval.protocol: mean of three seeds; ablations on En-De before unknown word replacement; GNMT numbers quoted from Wu et al.

availability.weights: source code and models available at fairseq (footnote 1)

limits: Speed comparison to GNMT is against numbers quoted from Wu et al. on different hardware (K80, 88-core CPU, TPU); authors note CPU speeds are not directly comparable and TPU not measured.
Training is expensive: 18.5 days single GPU for En-De, about 37 days on 8 GPUs for En-Fr.
Effective context of the En-Fr model is only 25 words; fixed receptive field and position embeddings impose a maximum sentence length.
Best single runs of mixture-of-experts LSTM (Shazeer) exceed ConvS2S best runs on En-De; ensemble results and RL not applied.
Variance scaling assumptions (equal variance of summands, uniform attention) are stated not to always hold.
Dropout rate, number of epochs, length-norm alpha and parameter counts are not stated.
Summarisation does not beat the best specialised RNN models.
Superseded by Transformer (Vaswani et al. 2017) shortly after; this paper uses no self-attention (inferred: not mentioned).
